summary: Recursively flattens a tree into a contiguous output array. Stores the current node pointer at out[a3], records the output index a3 into this[18] (offset 0x48), then recurses over up to four consecutive child pointers beginning at offset 0x4C (skipping null children) and finally over one extra child at offset 0x5C if non-null. Returns the next free output index.

operations.description: Write the output index a3 into this[18] (offset 0x48), recording where this node was placed.
Store the current node pointer at out[a3] in the output array, and compute the next output index as a3 + 1.
Iterate four times over child pointers starting at offset 0x4C; null children are skipped.
If the child pointer at the current cursor position is non-null, recurse into that child subtree.
Recursive call to linearize the child subtree into the remaining output slots, threading the running output index.
If the extra child pointer at this[23] (offset 0x5C) is non-null, recurse once more into it.
Recursive call to linearize the extra child subtree when the guard holds.
Return the final next free output index.

unresolved: Child pointer offsets 0x50, 0x54 and 0x58 (the remaining three loop slots) have no packet evidence reference; they are implied by the four-iteration loop beginning at 0x4C.
Whether the traversal order is pre-order and what the flattened array is later used for is DERIVED from existing analysis, not independently proven.
